limitations: Single sample for each scenario, not final performance acceptance.
Readers request the same 128-event pages but byte budgets return different work; raw readerWork is retained. Reader timing alone is not an equal-work latency comparison.
Workload uses long opaque IDs and direct low-level stream writes. It tests context churn in the new UUID-capable implementation but is not itself a production UUID-shape lifecycle workload.
The high-churn single-message staging stress exceeds the 1024-field final-entry manifest limit; it does not publish that oversized assistant header and is not a normal UI transcript.
Logical page bytes are writer cache-write-page deltas times page_size, not WAL frame/header traffic, checkpoint copies, fsync counts or physical device IO.
No admission backlog, native UI frames, input/cancel latency or physical power loss is simulated here.
No historical compression, VACUUM, increased commit interval or weakened FULL durability was used.
